correctness.rationale: The complete-graph one-body spectrum produces four nonoverlapping symmetric-cube energy sectors. The projected triple-occupancy Gram matrices have exact rank profile \(1,n-1,n,n\) for all \(n\ge3\), proving an explicit dark projector and \(\dim\mathcal D=\binom{n+2}{3}-3n\). Positivity of all site loss rates fixes the common kernel, and dissipativity proves asymptotic decay on its invariant orthogonal complement. Gram-inverse contractions give \(\eta_{(3)}=1\), \(\eta_{(2,1)}=(n^2-2n+2)/((n-1)(n^2-3n+3))\), and \(\eta_{(1,1,1)}=6(n-2)/((n-1)(n^2-3n+3))\), with ordering difference numerator \(-n^2+8n-14\). The symbolic all-size identity checker passed, and independent normalized Fock-basis checks passed at \(n=3,\ldots,8\) with unequal positive loss-rate spectral checks through \(n=6\). Finite tests corroborate rather than establish the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Three highly relevant before November 2016 primary manuscripts were compared at claim/implication level. Their general dark-state and three-body-loss frameworks do not evaluate the symmetric-cube complete-graph bright-rank sum, exact projector or three distinct occupancy survival laws. value.rationale: The problem is motivated by physical on-site three-body recombination and a canonical all-to-all network benchmark. The full exactly solvable three-boson Lindblad model reveals a nontrivial qualitative inversion between initially separated and initially partially co-located configurations between \(n=5\) and \(n=6\), as well as the rate-independent projection law for arbitrary initial states. The four-sector rank structure and exact rational fractions give interpretable collision-susceptibility tests for finite open quantum networks rather than a mere numerical instance or parameter substitution. The result is not claimed to describe interacting gases, finite-time rates or thermodynamic phases.
